title: Omytea Prediction Receipt
description: A tamper-evident record of one machine prediction: frozen before the fact, resolved by an independent source, mechanically scored. The canonical frozen payload is the JSON object containing the fields receipt_id, created_at, question, prediction, resolution_deadline, resolution_source (plus specimen and provenance, each only if present), serialized with json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True) and hashed with SHA-256 to produce frozen_hash. Anyone can recompute the hash and the scores from the receipt alone. Timeline ordering (created_at < resolution_deadline; created_at < outcome.resolved_at) cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and is enforced by the reference verifier, which also warns when outcome.resolved_at is after resolution_deadline.

created_at.description: Freeze time: when the prediction was committed, ISO 8601 UTC. Everything in the frozen payload was fixed at this moment. Must be strictly earlier than resolution_deadline.

question.description: Plain-language description of the target: what is being predicted, about what, over what window.

prediction.description: The frozen probabilistic prediction. Exactly one of `branches` (discrete outcome distribution) or `quantiles` (continuous outcome distribution).

branches.description: Discrete distribution over mutually exclusive outcome labels. Probabilities must sum to 1 (tolerance 1e-6).

quantiles.description: Continuous predictive distribution given as quantiles. `levels` are strictly increasing in (0,1); `values` are the corresponding non-decreasing quantile values.

resolution_deadline.description: Horizon: the time by which the outcome must be resolvable, ISO 8601 UTC.

resolution_source.description: How the outcome will be determined, independently of the predictor.

frozen_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical frozen payload (see the top-level description for the exact serialization).

outcome.description: The resolved outcome. Added at resolution time; absent while the prediction is pending. `label` for branch predictions, `value` for quantile predictions.

resolved_at.description: When the outcome was recorded, ISO 8601 UTC. Must be strictly later than created_at. A value after resolution_deadline is reported as a warning, not a failure: resolvers lag, and the verifier cannot tell lag from an outcome read outside the declared window.

scores.description: Mechanical scores of the frozen prediction against the resolved outcome. Recomputable by anyone from `prediction` + `outcome` alone. `brier` and `log_loss` for branch predictions; `crps` for quantile predictions. Lower is better for all.

baseline_scores.description: Scores of named reference forecasts (e.g. `uniform`, `persistence`) against the same outcome. Each baseline carries its own full distribution so its scores are recomputable from the receipt alone.

specimen.description: True if this receipt is an illustrative specimen, not a live track-record entry. Included in the frozen payload when present.

provenance.description: Issuer-declared origin of the prediction and outcome: `real` (a live prediction frozen before a real-world outcome resolved from the declared source), `synthetic` (generated or simulated data, not an observation of the world), or `fixture` (a test or demo artifact built to exercise the format). Included in the frozen payload when present, so it cannot be changed after freezing without breaking frozen_hash; a matching hash does not make the label true. Absent means unknown, as on every receipt that predates the field. A specimen receipt cannot declare `real`.

notes.description: Free-text annotation. NOT part of the frozen payload.
